exposure: Antenatal corticosteroids (ACS) administration timing (optimally timed: >24h and <7 days, mistimed: >7 days pre-delivery, no ACS)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 250 women delivering before 35 weeks' gestation with a diagnosis of preterm pre-eclampsia.
finding: Optimal antenatal corticosteroid administration was poor, with the largest group receiving ACS more than 7 days prior to birth, and non-receipt of ACS was associated with a higher rate of intrauterine fetal death.
mod_finding: There was an increase in vaginal delivery and a reduction in caesarean section in the group of women who did not receive ACS.
